Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Clinical summary (from transcript): 26-year-old male with known asthma and atopy (hayfever, dust allergy) presents with ~3 hours of chest tightness, mild shortness of breath (worse on exertion/stairs, not at rest), wheeze and non-productive cough after a recent upper respiratory infection last week. Has been without his inhaled steroid and salbutamol for ~1 week. Prior severe asthma requiring intubation in adolescence. Currently not reporting severe distress.
- Key concerns: Acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by recent viral URTI and medication omission; patient anxious given prior intubation.
- Diagnostic reasoning (DDx concordant with transcript):
  - Acute asthma exacerbation due to infective/allergic trigger and running out of inhalers — High likelihood (supported by known asthma, wheeze, URTI, missed inhalers).
  - Viral bronchitis / post-viral reactive airways — Moderate likelihood (recent cold with persistent cough/wheeze; can overlap with asthma exacerbation).
  - Community-acquired pneumonia — Low to moderate likelihood (possible after URTI but no fever, productive sputum or focal signs documented).
- Conflict(s) between transcript and DDx: None noted

Management Plan
- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded:
  - Prescriptions to be sent for inhalers (salbutamol/Ventolin and Clenil Modulite) — instructions documented: Clenil Modulite for ongoing use (morning), Ventolin as needed (PRN). Specific inhaler dose/administration frequency not fully documented for prescriptions.
  - Oral corticosteroid tablets prescribed; instructed to take two tablets in the morning for 5 days — specific steroid name not documented.
  - Spacer prescribed and will be sent with instructions; patient advised on spacer use (priming, several breaths).
  - Safety-netting: seek urgent medical attention for any deterioration (worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, light-headedness); seek care if needing Ventolin more frequently than every 3 hours.
  - Advice: rest and consider time off work (doctor advised; patient may self-certify first 7 days).
  - Follow-up: advised to see a clinician if symptoms worsen or Ventolin use is frequent; no specific scheduled follow-up documented.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- 1) Acute asthma exacerbation (High) — Justification: Known asthma with prior severe exacerbation; current wheeze, chest tightness and SOB after recent URTI; missed inhaled steroid and salbutamol for ~1 week. Strongest diagnosis aligned with transcript.
- 2) Viral bronchitis / post-viral reactive airways (Moderate) — Justification: Recent cold last week with lingering cough and wheeze; can cause or exacerbate airway hyperreactivity in atopic patients.
- 3) Community-acquired pneumonia (Low–Moderate) — Justification: Post-viral bacterial pneumonia possible but lacks supporting features in history (no fever, no productive sputum, no focal chest pain or exam recorded).
